slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The Data Landscapers review (an AI-assisted compilation) states that rural schools in Burkina Faso are predominantly paper-based, with data aggregated and digitised at district level, and that it found no evidence of digital tools for direct entry of attendance, enrolment or grades in rural primary schools; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The Data Landscapers review (an AI-assisted compilation) states that limited pilots such as the FIUE-BF student database exist but are not widespread in rural areas, giving no count of schools; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

facts.fact: La Tribune du Faso, from the digital transition ministry's communications office, reports that on 25 June 2025 the two ministers reviewed work on the national pupil file, online enrolment and school identity cards, with a roadmap still awaited and progressive enrolment of pupils due to start at the next school year; no school is said to be using it.
The article states that the national platform is meant to follow pupils from primary school to university, and that enrolment had not begun at 25 June 2025.

The article states that the national pupil file is being built by the technical teams of the ministry of digital transition and the ministry of basic education, whose ministers reviewed it on 25 June 2025.
The article states that the design and implementation of the national pupil platform has the technical and financial support of the WURI project; it names no domestic budget line.

systems.owner: ministry of basic education with the ministry of digital transition; WURI project support
systems.tiers: in preparation at June 2025; intended from primary to university, with online enrolment and school identity cards

note: Classed emis as a learner register (a national file of pupils filled by enrolment); the article does not say whether schools do the enrolling.

facts.fact: The World Bank appraisal document of 14 April 2025 states that the project will support the design and deployment of a centralised digital platform for student management and monitoring, with a smartphone application for data collection at school level and a web interface for the central administration; it is still to be designed and no school is said to use it.
The appraisal document describes the student management platform as a future deployment under a project for pre-primary and primary education, and reports it in use at no level at 14 April 2025.

The appraisal document calls the planned platform a key step towards complete digitisation of student records, and states that key education data and information are currently stored mainly as hard copies; no date is given, so the document's date is used.

The appraisal document names the Ministry of Basic Education (MEBAPLN) as implementing agency of the project that will build the student management platform, which is to be the student management module of the Education Management Information System.

The appraisal document places the student management platform under Component 3 of the project (US$42.7 million: US$17.7 million IDA and US$25.0 million GPE), within a US$203.1 million operation financed by IDA and the GPE fund; it names no domestic budget line for the platform.

It states only that the project (P502472) was not yet effective on 12 March 2026, with nothing disbursed, and that the GPE envelope was cut from US$53.1 million to US$39.7 million at the November 2025 restructuring; neither statement is tied in this document to a system, so no fact.
